# GENERATED FILE -- see generate_war_parties_mod.py. Do not hand-edit.
#
# Collects the countries fighting on each side of a war, up to 64 per side, and
# each one's cumulative shadow-attrition figure at that moment. The war and
# declaration slot banks copy these globals into their permanent slots, the same
# way balance_battle_comp_side feeds bcw0..bcl9.
#
# Why it exists: the war log used to keep only four countries -- attacker,
# defender, winner, loser -- so a war of five against five recorded two of them
# and the ledger had to guess the rest from the battle log. Worse, "what this
# war cost country X" could only be answered for those two, and only by
# differencing their lifetime counters, which silently included any other war
# they were in and any month they stayed in after making a separate peace.
#
# With this, every participant carries its own before-and-after, so the ledger
# subtracts per country instead of per war leader.
#
# Called in WAR scope, once at on_war_declared and once at on_ending_war.
#
#   global_var:wpan / wpdn     how many were found on each side -- the TRUE
#                              count even when it is larger than 64, so a
#                              truncated record says so rather than lying about
#                              the size of the war
#   global_var:wpa0..wpa63      the attacking countries
#   global_var:wqa0..wqa63      each one's shadow_attr at that moment
#   global_var:wpd0..wpd63      the defending countries
#   global_var:wqd0..wqd63      each one's shadow_attr at that moment
#
# THE CAPACITY WAS 10, AND 10 WAS MEASURED AS TOO FEW. The Tuscan war against
# France ended with 15 attackers and 14 defenders, so five countries fell off
# the record -- Switzerland among them, which the player had called into the war
# personally. 64 is not a ceiling either: a Tibetan war in the same campaign
# ended with 32 defenders. Anything wider than this belongs in a per-row bank
# like bpart rather than in fixed columns.
#
# A country that has never run the monthly pulse has no shadow_attr yet; it is
# read as 0 rather than skipped, so the pairing by slot index stays intact.

balance_war_parties = {
